weeks.title: Six family favourites
weeks.note: The previous family menu: six meals including burgers. The weekday sequence is a reconstruction, rather than a recorded schedule.

honey-mustard-chicken-mash.title: Creamy Honey-Mustard Chicken with Mash & Greens
honey-mustard-chicken-mash.shortTitle: Creamy Honey-Mustard Chicken with Mash & Greens
honey-mustard-chicken-mash.subtitle: Golden chicken breast in a mild mustard sauce with buttery mash and greens.
steps: Prepare mash
Peel and chop potatoes. Boil in salted water for 15–18 minutes until tender. Drain and mash with butter and warmed milk.
Cook the chicken
Cut chicken breasts into even thin fillets; season lightly. Brown in oil over medium-high heat for 3–4 minutes per side, then cook to 75°C in the centre. Set aside.
Make the sauce
In the same pan, soften crushed garlic for 30 seconds. Add stock, Dijon, wholegrain mustard and honey. Simmer 2–3 minutes and return chicken to coat. Thin with water if needed.
Serve the greens
Steam broccoli and beans for 4–5 minutes until bright and tender. Serve with mash and chicken, spooning over the sauce.
honey-mustard-chicken-mash.family: Offer sauce on the side for anyone who prefers their chicken plain.
honey-mustard-chicken-mash.kidJob: Help wash and portion the vegetables with adult supervision.
honey-mustard-chicken-mash.allergens: Milk and mustard; check stock ingredients.
honey-mustard-chicken-mash.variation: Adjust carbohydrates and vegetables to each person's appetite.
honey-mustard-chicken-mash.prepTip: Chop potatoes and wash beans ahead; keep everything refrigerated.

nutrition.note: High-protein chicken breast with comforting mash and greens.

teriyaki-salmon-chicken-bowls.title: Teriyaki Salmon & Chicken Rice Bowls
teriyaki-salmon-chicken-bowls.subtitle: Sweet soy-glazed salmon for some and chicken breast for the kids, with rice and crunchy vegetables.
steps: Rice and vegetables
Cook rice using packet instructions. Thinly slice cucumber and carrot, cut avocado and steam broccoli.
Mix teriyaki
Mix soy, honey, vinegar, grated ginger, crushed garlic, sesame oil and 3 tablespoons of water. Set the sauce aside in a clean bowl.
Cook separately
Pan-cook salmon until opaque and cooked to preference. Fry sliced chicken separately to 75°C, keeping utensils separate to avoid fish cross-contact.
Glaze and assemble
Simmer the sauce in a clean pan; thicken with cornflour mixed with a splash of cold water. Coat salmon and chicken separately. Serve over rice with fresh vegetables and broccoli.
teriyaki-salmon-chicken-bowls.family: Cook chicken breast instead of salmon for Phoebe and Tobias; give everyone the same teriyaki glaze.
teriyaki-salmon-chicken-bowls.kidJob: Wash cucumber, portion rice and arrange vegetables.
teriyaki-salmon-chicken-bowls.allergens: Soy, fish, and possible wheat in soy sauce. Use separate utensils for fish and chicken.
teriyaki-salmon-chicken-bowls.variation: Adjust carbohydrates and vegetables to each person's appetite.
teriyaki-salmon-chicken-bowls.prepTip: Mix sauce and cut vegetables ahead.

nutrition.note: Protein and calories depend on the chosen salmon/chicken mix.

beef-mushroom-stroganoff.title: Creamy Beef & Mushroom Stroganoff with Egg Noodles
beef-mushroom-stroganoff.shortTitle: Creamy Beef & Mushroom Stroganoff with Egg Noodles
beef-mushroom-stroganoff.subtitle: Tender beef strips and mushrooms in a quick creamy sauce with egg noodles.
steps: Cook the noodles
Cook egg noodles in boiling water according to packet instructions; reserve some cooking water.
Sear the beef
Pat strips dry. Sear in batches in a hot oiled pan 1–2 minutes per side, then remove to keep tender.
Make mushroom sauce
Cook sliced mushrooms and onion in butter for 5–6 minutes. Add crushed garlic, paprika and mustard for 30 seconds. Add stock and Worcestershire; simmer 3–4 minutes.
Finish gently
Reduce heat, stir in sour cream and return beef to warm through. Do not boil the cream sauce. Adjust with reserved noodle water and toss with noodles.
beef-mushroom-stroganoff.family: Serve mushrooms separately for fussy eaters.
beef-mushroom-stroganoff.kidJob: Help wash and portion the vegetables with adult supervision.
beef-mushroom-stroganoff.allergens: Milk, egg, wheat/gluten, mustard, possible fish in Worcestershire.
beef-mushroom-stroganoff.variation: Adjust carbohydrates and vegetables to each person's appetite.
beef-mushroom-stroganoff.prepTip: Slice beef and mushrooms before school pick-up.

nutrition.note: Lean beef provides iron and protein; serve with extra greens if desired.

bbq-pork-pineapple-wraps.title: BBQ Pork & Pineapple Wraps with Crunchy Slaw
bbq-pork-pineapple-wraps.shortTitle: BBQ Pork & Pineapple Wraps with Crunchy Slaw
bbq-pork-pineapple-wraps.subtitle: Fast BBQ pork, juicy pineapple and fresh crunchy slaw in soft wraps.
steps: Prepare the crunch
Toss slaw mix with sliced cucumber. Stir yoghurt with vinegar and a little honey; dress at the last minute.
Sear the pork
Slice pork into thin strips, season with paprika and crushed garlic. Stir-fry in hot oil for 4–6 minutes until browned and thoroughly cooked.
Make it sticky
Add drained pineapple pieces to the pan for a minute. Stir in barbecue sauce and remaining honey, coating the pork.
Fill the wraps
Warm soft wraps. Divide pork and pineapple between wraps, add crunchy slaw and serve any extra sauce on the side.
bbq-pork-pineapple-wraps.family: Put pineapple, pork and slaw in separate bowls for everyone to choose.
bbq-pork-pineapple-wraps.kidJob: Help wash and portion the vegetables with adult supervision.
bbq-pork-pineapple-wraps.allergens: Wheat/gluten and milk. Check barbecue sauce and wrap labels.
bbq-pork-pineapple-wraps.variation: Adjust carbohydrates and vegetables to each person's appetite.
bbq-pork-pineapple-wraps.prepTip: Make the yoghurt dressing and slice pork ahead.

nutrition.note: Amounts assume two soft wraps per serving.

chicken-egg-fried-rice.title: Chicken & Egg Fried Rice
chicken-egg-fried-rice.subtitle: Golden chicken, soft egg, peas and carrots in tasty soy-oyster fried rice.
steps: Get the rice ready
Cook rice ahead and chill promptly in a shallow container; keep refrigerated until cooking. Do not leave cooked rice at room temperature.
Cook chicken and eggs
Dice chicken and stir-fry until golden and 75°C internally. Remove. Scramble beaten eggs in the pan and set aside.
Fry vegetables and rice
Cook diced carrots for 3 minutes in oil, then add peas, garlic and grated ginger. Add cold cooked rice and stir-fry until thoroughly hot.
Finish and serve
Stir through soy, oyster sauce, vinegar and sesame oil. Return chicken and egg, toss until steaming hot and top with spring onion.
chicken-egg-fried-rice.family: Serve toppings and sauce separately so the kids can build their own plates.
chicken-egg-fried-rice.kidJob: Whisk eggs and wash spring onions.
chicken-egg-fried-rice.allergens: Egg, soy, wheat/gluten in sauces and molluscs in oyster sauce.
chicken-egg-fried-rice.variation: Adjust carbohydrates and vegetables to each person's appetite.
chicken-egg-fried-rice.prepTip: Cool rice quickly and refrigerate; reheat until steaming hot.

nutrition.note: Rice quantity is dry weight before cooking.

family-beef-cheeseburgers.title: Family Beef Cheeseburgers with Salad
family-beef-cheeseburgers.subtitle: Juicy beef patties with melted cheese, lettuce, tomato and pickles.
steps: Shape the patties
Divide beef mince into five patties slightly larger than burger buns. Season the outside just before cooking.
Cook burgers
Sear in a pan or barbecue over medium-high heat for about 4–5 minutes a side, until cooked through to 75°C internally. Add cheese for the last minute.
Prepare toppings
Wash and slice lettuce, tomatoes, onion and pickles. Toast buns briefly and stir tomato sauce with a little Dijon.
Let everyone build
Put buns, patties, cheese, salad and sauce on the table so everyone builds their own burger. Serve with fresh salad or optional chips.
family-beef-cheeseburgers.family: Serve toppings and sauce separately so the kids can build their own plates.
family-beef-cheeseburgers.allergens: Wheat/gluten, milk, mustard; check bun and sauce labels.
family-beef-cheeseburgers.variation: Adjust carbohydrates and vegetables to each person's appetite.
family-beef-cheeseburgers.prepTip: Shape patties ahead and refrigerate covered.

nutrition.note: Estimates exclude optional chips and extra toppings.

weeks.title: Five nights. Big flavours.
weeks.note: The family’s locked-in lineup. Fresh, colourful and very much worth gathering around.

mediterranean-beef.title: Mediterranean Beef & Couscous Bowls
mediterranean-beef.subtitle: Lemony couscous, warmly spiced beef and all the fresh things.
steps: Fluff things up
Put the couscous in a heatproof bowl. Add boiling water using the packet’s couscous-to-water ratio, cover and stand for the packet time, then fluff with a fork. Stir through half the lemon juice.
Chop the crunch
Dice the cucumbers and halve the tomatoes. Crush the garlic. Mix the yoghurt with the remaining lemon juice and half the garlic. Keep chilled until serving.
Bring on the beef

Heat the oil in a large frying pan over medium-high heat. Cook the mince for 8–10 minutes, breaking it up. Stir in cumin, oregano, remaining garlic, salt and pepper for the last 2 minutes. Check the mince reaches 75°C in the centre.
Build your own bowl
Divide the couscous, beef and salad between bowls. Crumble over feta and add the lemon yoghurt. Let everyone keep their favourite bits separate if they like.
mediterranean-beef.family: Serve the salad and yoghurt in little bowls so everyone can build their own. For milder plates, put a little cooked beef aside before adding spices.
mediterranean-beef.kidJob: Crumble the feta and fluff the cooled couscous with a fork, with an adult nearby.

nutrition.note: Fresh vegetables add crunch and fibre; lean beef contributes iron. Wholemeal couscous is an easy fibre swap.

mediterranean-beef.allergens: Wheat/gluten and milk. Check couscous, yoghurt and spice packaging.
mediterranean-beef.variation: Use cooked lentils instead of beef for a meat-free version; amounts and nutrition will change.
mediterranean-beef.prepTip: Chop the salad and mix the yoghurt earlier in the day; refrigerate separately.

pork-tonkatsu.title: Japanese Pork Tonkatsu with Crunchy Slaw & Sweet Potato Wedges
pork-tonkatsu.subtitle: Golden panko pork, rainbow slaw and sweet potato wedges.
steps: Wedges first

Heat the oven to 200°C fan-forced. Cut the sweet potato into even wedges, toss with one-third of the oil and a pinch of the measured salt. Spread over a lined tray and roast for 30–35 minutes, turning halfway, until tender.
Make it crunchy
Finely shred the cabbage and grate the carrots. Toss with yoghurt and vinegar; refrigerate. Stir the barbecue, soy and Worcestershire sauces together in a separate serving bowl.
Crumb the pork

Pat the pork dry and flatten to an even 1 cm thickness. Put flour, beaten egg and panko in three shallow bowls. Season the flour with remaining salt and pepper. Coat pork in flour, then egg, then crumbs. Discard unused coating that touched raw pork.
Golden hour

Heat remaining oil in a large pan over medium heat. Cook the pork for about 4–5 minutes per side, in batches, until golden and cooked through; check the thickest part reaches 75°C. Lower the heat if the crumb browns too fast. Rest 3 minutes, slice and serve with slaw, wedges and sauce on the side.
pork-tonkatsu.family: Keep the sauce separate for little dippers. Serve raw carrot sticks instead of dressed slaw for anyone who prefers it.
pork-tonkatsu.kidJob: Mix the slaw dressing and set out little sauce bowls. An adult handles raw pork and the hot pan.

nutrition.note: Sweet potato and cabbage bring colour and fibre. A shallow fry keeps the crumb crisp; actual absorbed oil varies.

pork-tonkatsu.allergens: Wheat/gluten, egg, milk, soy and possibly fish in Worcestershire sauce. Check all sauce labels.
pork-tonkatsu.variation: Chicken breast works too: flatten evenly and check it reaches 75°C. Use fish-free Worcestershire if needed; check the label.
pork-tonkatsu.prepTip: Cut the wedges and shred the slaw first. Keep raw meat and salad utensils separate.

burrito-bowls.title: Loaded Beef Burrito Bowls
burrito-bowls.subtitle: Smoky beef, rice, black beans and a choose-your-own topping party.
steps: Rice on, music on
Cook the rice following packet directions. Brown rice may take longer; start it first. Drain and rinse the black beans and corn.
Get the toppings ready
Shred the lettuce, halve the tomatoes, dice the avocado and cut the lime into wedges. Dice the onion and crush the garlic.
Make the smoky middle

Heat the oil in a large pan. Soften the onion for 4 minutes. Add mince, breaking it up for 8–10 minutes, then garlic, cumin, paprika, salt and pepper. Stir for 1 minute. Add beans, corn and a splash of water. Simmer until hot throughout and the mince reaches 75°C.
Load ’em up
Spoon rice and beef into bowls. Add lettuce, tomatoes, avocado, cheddar, yoghurt and salsa. Finish with a squeeze of lime. Keep salsa mild and let grown-ups add their own heat.
burrito-bowls.family: A toppings bar is the whole point. Keep a few beans and some corn separate before they go into the beef.
burrito-bowls.kidJob: Wash and tear the lettuce, then arrange the topping bowls.

nutrition.note: Black beans add fibre and plant protein. Adjust rice and toppings to appetite rather than expecting identical portions.

burrito-bowls.allergens: Milk. Check salsa and spice labels for additional allergens.
burrito-bowls.variation: For a lighter appetite, use a smaller rice portion and more lettuce. For meat-free bowls, replace beef with extra beans; quantities will differ.
burrito-bowls.prepTip: Cook the beef-and-bean mixture ahead and refrigerate promptly. Reheat until steaming hot throughout.

italian-chicken-pasta.title: Fresh Italian Chicken, Zucchini & Tomato Pasta
italian-chicken-pasta.subtitle: Juicy tomatoes, golden chicken, basil and lemon. No cream required.
steps: Get the pasta going
Bring a large pot of water to the boil and cook pasta following packet directions. Before draining, save a mug of the cooking water.
Prep the fresh bits
Slice the zucchini into half-moons, halve the tomatoes and crush the garlic. Zest and juice the lemon. Cut chicken into even bite-sized pieces using a separate board.
Golden chicken, juicy tomatoes

Heat half the oil in a large pan. Cook chicken for 7–10 minutes, turning, until its centre reaches 75°C. Transfer to a clean plate. Add remaining oil, zucchini and tomatoes to the pan and cook 5–6 minutes. Stir in garlic and oregano for 1 minute.
Toss it all together

Return chicken to the pan with pasta and spinach. Add lemon zest, half the juice, salt, pepper and a splash of pasta water. Toss until spinach wilts and everything is hot. Add torn basil and parmesan. Taste before adding more lemon juice.
italian-chicken-pasta.family: Keep some plain pasta aside before tossing. Finely grate zucchini into the sauce for anyone who prefers smaller veggie pieces.
italian-chicken-pasta.kidJob: Tear the basil leaves and sprinkle the parmesan at the table.

nutrition.note: Chicken provides protein and the tomato-zucchini mix adds vegetables. Wholemeal pasta can increase fibre.

italian-chicken-pasta.allergens: Wheat/gluten and milk; some pasta contains egg. Check the packet.
italian-chicken-pasta.variation: Use gluten-free pasta or skip parmesan if needed, checking every product label. These swaps alter nutrition.
italian-chicken-pasta.prepTip: Slice vegetables ahead. Keep raw chicken covered on the lowest fridge shelf.

sweet-chilli-bowls.title: Sweet Chilli & Soy Salmon/Chicken Bowls
sweet-chilli-bowls.subtitle: Sticky glaze, fluffy rice and bright greens. Salmon, chicken, or a bit of both.
steps: Start with the rice
Cook rice following packet directions. Cut broccoli into small florets, make carrot ribbons with a peeler and slice the cucumber. Finely grate ginger and crush garlic.
Stir up the sticky sauce

Mix sweet chilli sauce, soy, ginger, garlic and half the lime juice. Reserve half in a clean bowl for serving BEFORE anything touches raw meat or fish. Discard any sauce left after contact with raw protein.
Choose your Friday

Salmon: brush with a little oil and the cooking half of the glaze, then bake at 200°C fan-forced for around 12–15 minutes, depending on thickness, until opaque and flaking easily; check for bones. Chicken: cut into even strips and pan-fry in the oil for 7–10 minutes, turning, until the centre reaches 75°C; add the cooking glaze in the final 2 minutes. Mixed: divide oil and cooking glaze between the proteins, cook separately and use separate utensils.
Make it a bowl night

Steam broccoli for 4–5 minutes until just tender. Divide rice, protein, broccoli, carrot and cucumber into bowls. Add the reserved clean sauce and remaining lime to taste. For mixed plates, give each person their chosen protein.
sweet-chilli-bowls.family: Pick salmon, chicken or half-and-half above. For less heat, keep a portion of protein unglazed and offer sauce at the table.
sweet-chilli-bowls.kidJob: Arrange cucumber and carrot ribbons in the bowls. An adult handles the peeler and checks fish for bones.

nutrition.note: Salmon supplies omega-3 fats. Chicken is a leaner alternative. The vegetable mix adds colour, texture and fibre.

sweet-chilli-bowls.allergens: Soy and usually wheat/gluten in soy sauce; fish when salmon is selected. Check sweet chilli and soy labels. Mixed preparation is not suitable for avoiding fish cross-contact.
sweet-chilli-bowls.variation: Use reduced-salt tamari if avoiding wheat, checking it is labelled gluten-free. Sauce quantities are deliberately moderate; add to taste.
sweet-chilli-bowls.prepTip: Make the glaze ahead and refrigerate. Keep the serving half separate from raw protein.

weeks.title: Six easy dinners. Proper good food.
weeks.note: No pork, one wrap night, plenty of vegetables and generous protein. Kym-friendly prep with a proper weekend Aussie BBQ.
